result.summary: This is a full H-bridge circuit using four thyristors (Th1, Th2, Th3, Th4) and four antiparallel diodes (D1, D2, D3, D4) to control the direction and magnitude of current through a load. The input voltage V is applied across the top and bottom rails. The load is connected between the two midpoint nodes of the H-bridge. Current flows through the load in one direction when Th1 and Th4 are conducting, and in the opposite direction when Th2 and Th3 are conducting. The diodes provide a freewheeling path for inductive loads.
result.topology: The H-bridge consists of two legs. The top leg has Th1 and Th3, with D1 and D3 as antiparallel diodes. The bottom leg has Th2 and Th4, with D2 and D4 as antiparallel diodes. The load is connected between the midpoints of the two legs (N3 and N4). The input voltage V is applied across the top and bottom rails. The diodes provide a freewheeling path for inductive loads.
design_notes: This is a full H-bridge circuit. The thyristors are typically controlled by a microcontroller or other logic circuit to switch the current direction through the load.
